legacyClaimPolicy: FluentCart 1.3.9 booted and served its REST index on the isolated matrix below, so runtime support may now be claimed. Any claim must cite the 324-operation runtime fixture, never the 342-operation specification: the specification documents 27 operations that 1.3.9 does not serve.

captureMatrix.note: Plan 03 pins WordPress sha256:ffef0dca… and labels it 7.0.2. That digest is actually WordPress 6.9.1. Captures were taken on the digest that really is 7.0.2 so each fixture matches the version its profile records. A control run of both isolated captures on sha256:ffef0dca… (6.9.1) produced an identical route set, so the WordPress version does not affect the FluentCart namespace.

profiles.description: Specification evidence for the oldest documented FluentCart
FluentCart core 1.5.5 with Pro 1.5.4 and nothing else
Every plugin active on the local playground

equivalence.method: The superseded all-active capture (WordPress 7.0.2, eleven active plugins) was compared pair by pair against the isolated core+Pro capture. Both contain the same 386 canonical operations: nothing added, nothing removed. No other plugin on the playground contributes a fluent-cart/v2 route, so one fixture is honest evidence for both profiles.

profiles.description: FluentCart 1.3.9 booted in isolation and indexed at run time

specificationDelta.note: Stale operations are documented but no longer served. The 61 current operations absent from the specification are served but undocumented, so no tool may cite the specification as evidence for them.

specificationAgainstItsOwnRuntime.note: Measured against the very runtime the specification claims to describe. The specification is not runtime evidence even for its own version.

legacyToCurrentCore.note: The first runtime-to-runtime core delta this project holds. Every earlier 1.3.9-to-1.5.5 figure compared a specification with a runtime.

proOverCore.note: Operations attributable to FluentCart Pro 1.5.4 alone: 386 minus 355.

abilityParity.bridgePolicy: Opt-in and read-only. Runtime discovery intersects the captured exact-name allowlist with category=fluent-cart and meta.annotations.readOnlyHint=true. Unknown, missing and write abilities are never exposed.
abilityParity.adapterDisposition: The external MCP adapter was absent and was not installed for the audit. The optional bridge uses the public WordPress Abilities REST endpoints directly.

executionMethodEvidence.reason: FluentCart supplied meta.annotations.readOnlyHint=true but no WordPress readonly annotation. WordPress therefore rejected GET and executed the same read through POST.

rows.semanticDifference: Both add an order note; the standalone write is classified irreversible because FluentCart exposes no supported note removal.
Both change label assignments; no exact read-back plus restore contract has been proven for this write.
The native ability changes one order; the standalone bulk status route is destructive and deliberately unavailable.
The native ability covers several lifecycle transitions; standalone cancellation is unavailable in every write mode until a cleanable acceptance lane proves it.
Both return customer detail; the native ability additionally offers bounded optional orders, subscriptions, addresses, labels and notes in one call.
Standalone inventory is split across catalogue and pricing reads; the native ability provides one inventory-oriented projection.
Both return one order; their response projections are independently owned and not asserted byte-equivalent.
The native ability is order-scoped; the standalone activity list is a general activity endpoint.
Both return one product; their projections are independently owned and not asserted byte-equivalent.
No standalone tool combines one-time performance, forward subscription metrics and an optional payment schedule.
Standalone exposes raw report routes; the native ability owns a semantic refund report contract.
Both answer period sales, but standalone adds explicit scope, currency and warning metadata verified against orders.
Both return a time series; standalone explicitly reports requested versus applied granularity and scope warnings.
Standalone documents its reviewed search abstraction; native returns FluentCart's current advanced-query schema.
Both orient the caller; standalone derives capability claims from its filtered REST tool registry.
Both return one subscription; their response projections are independently owned and not asserted byte-equivalent.
Both rank products; standalone states its units-sold ranking, scope and title-history caveat.
Standalone exposes a raw renewal report; native provides a bounded schedule with product, variation, currency and bucket controls.
Standalone additionally derives scheduled and expired status from coupon dates.
Both list customers; standalone documents cross-currency LTV and AOV limitations.
Both list orders; standalone documents the ignored customer_id behaviour and a supported customer-order alternative.
Both list products; standalone search is verified to include variation names.
Both provide reference data; standalone response is cached per authorised principal and route profile for at most 60 seconds.
Both list subscriptions; standalone documents minor-unit money and FluentCart's incomplete status filter.
Standalone transactions require one order; native can query the store ledger by order, subscription, customer, gateway, currency, mode and date.
Standalone create and update are reversible-policy writes; native also owns action semantics not automatically admitted by that proof.
Standalone offers reviewed filters and projections; native owns FluentCart's current metric and dimension vocabulary.
Standalone offers reviewed filters and projections; native owns FluentCart's current metric and dimension vocabulary.
Native adds product financial dimensions and metrics including discounts, refunds and order type.
Standalone exposes the raw sources report; native owns a structured query contract.
Standalone offers reviewed filters and projections; native owns FluentCart's current subscription metric and dimension vocabulary.
Both move money. Standalone execution remains unavailable because no cleanable live acceptance lane exists.
Standalone separates create and update so each operation retains its own idempotency and rollback contract.
